reason: The bacterial fragments and one lymphocyte have matching shapes, and the introduction says recognizing antigens helps start the response.

effect: The matching lymphocyte is active; the lymph node's time strip suggests it can now multiply there.

reason: The lymph node picture shows an activated cell dividing in its living tissue.

effect: The activated cell produced antibody-making cells and memory cells in the lymph node. Amino acids may now help make the antibody proteins.
reaction: It was useful to see that the descendants have two different roles.
reason: Antibodies are proteins, and earlier chapters showed amino acids are protein building blocks.
expectation: The antibody-making cells will use the amino acids to produce antibodies.

effect: The cells made antibodies whose tips match the bacteria's surface knobs.
reaction: The matching shapes make the next connection clear.
reason: Coating bacteria is a goal, and the antibody tips match their surface knobs.
expectation: The antibodies will bind to and coat the bacteria.

effect: The antibodies coated the bacteria, completing the first goal. The remaining goal is to give the body immune memory.
reaction: The matching tips made the coating easy to follow.
reason: The lymphocyte descendants include memory cells, so connecting them to the body seems like the next step.
expectation: The body will gain the memory lymphocytes produced in the lymph node.

effect: The body now contains memory lymphocytes, which can make a later response to the same antigen faster and larger. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The explanation made the purpose of the memory cells clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Growing the activated lymphocyte in the node was most worthwhile: its descendants had two distinct roles, making antibodies and providing memory.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the memory cells to the body felt like a fairly predictable final fitting, although its result explained why memory matters.

surprise.text: I didn't expect one activated lymphocyte to produce both antibody-making cells and lasting memory cells.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary. The lymph node's picture showed why the activated cell belonged there, though the details of the help from neighboring cells weren't explained.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter: matching the shapes was straightforward, but seeing how the response leads to memory gave the sequence a useful payoff.
